title: Wasm Curves
objective: Port moderate-domain elliptic L-series batches and plotting kernels to a shared Wasm-compatible core; classify specialist elliptic and hyperelliptic dependencies with tested portable fallbacks

oracles: desktop ecLseriesValues packed and decimal contracts
ordinary exhaustive hyperelliptic local-factor and Jacobian algorithms
exceptions: eclib, smalljac, and rforest remain specialist desktop-only dependencies with explicit portable fallbacks

handoff.summary: Implemented a host-neutral packed elliptic L-series Wasm adapter with exact decimal-ball and explicit binary64 plot transports, a JS backend matching ecLseriesValues plan/value/plot modes, a source-preserving core extractor, bounded resource contracts, and reviewed specialist curve dependency dispositions.
risks: The shared Wasm build and architecture inventories must add the new source, exports, backend merge, and classifications in the integration lane.
The first release leaves far-right direct-series acceleration on the existing ordinary fallback and limits each packed plot tile to 10000 points.
next_steps: Materialize ellipticLseriesCoreSource(packages/flint/src/elliptic_lfunction.c) into dist and compile it with src/curves/elliptic-lseries-adapter.c.
Export every sagejs_wasm_ec_lseries_* symbol, merge createCurveBackend(instance) into runtime.flint_backend(), and publish the curve backend files.
Classify the new C/header and Wasm boundaries, then run the real Chromium E37 L-series and complex-plot fixtures.
